children: India's food regulator has initiated legal action against Nestle India
over infant nutrition products after finding alleged violations related to product claims and quality standards, according to a social media post by the regulator.

The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) said it examined infant nutrition products and promotional materials available on e-commerce platforms and found that claims made for NAN Excella Pro Stage 1 and Lactogen Pro 1 did not comply with regulations governing the promotion of infant foods.

FSSAI said tests found a sample of a follow-up infant formula to be sub-standard for biotin content, with a referral laboratory later confirming non-compliance with prescribed requirements under infant nutrition rules.
Nestle India did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
Shares of the company were down 2.5% as of 1:20 p.m. IST.

FSSAI's action comes as Indian food authorities have stepped up scrutiny of food safety standards, product labelling and marketing claims, with the regulator increasing enforcement across packaged foods and infant nutrition products in recent years.
